sections.text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः।
The godless do not know how to act or how to renounce. They have neither purity nor truth. They do not understand the right principles of conduct.
They say the universe is an accident with no purpose and no God. Life is created by sexual union, a product of lust and nothing else.
Thinking thus, these degraded souls, these enemies of mankind - whose intelligence is negligible and whose deeds are monstrous - come into the world only to destroy.

So we had been discussing chapter 16, Deva Asura Sampat Vibhag Yoga, Yoga of Divine and Devilish Estates. So as per some of the commentators, this chapter from 16 onwards, except 16, 17, 18 are elaboration on the ideas which are already discussed in Bhagavad Gita previously. But now we are elaborating on those ideas so that we can understand and apply in our daily life.
The idea which we have seen earlier in the Bhagavad Gita is that the soul is divine, your self is divine. But the imposition on the self by all the layers which you have acquired through interactions with the Prakriti is hiding that self from you. I cant recognize myself right now because of all the layering on this pristine self.
So we have talked about who I, the individual, am. We talked about who the pristine self is. Now we are talking about what created this layering.
In chapter 15 we talked about the Supreme Purusha. The Purushottama is beyond perishable and imperishable. This body is perishable.
The self is imperishable. The equipment which I have to transact with this world, this body, this mind, this intellectual are perishable. But the one who is supporting this equipment using this equipment is imperishable.
Then Bhagawan said that I am even higher than them both the conditioned self in me which I consider my soul, my self is imperishable and perishable self that I condition myself, my body, my intellect are the two perishable me and imperishable me. Beyond this is the Supreme Me which transcends both Me the perishable and Me the imperishable. Those are the ideas we have seen in chapter 15.
And then in chapter 15 we also learned how that all pervading, imperishable became an individual soul. Its a portion of mine which is as eternal as my real self. When associated with this world of Prakriti then acquires five senses in mind then it enjoys the world of objects through those five senses and then gathering those experiences it creates its own personality.
Now, while interacting with this Prakriti, I gain both types of experiences -- experiences which are conducive and experiences which are non-conducive. The tendencies which I acquire become my wealth. So when we say my wealth in our day-to-day life, it is all that I earned and acquired.
Now that has become my estate, its my portfolio. So this chapter says I as the individual going through the variety of experiences from the day my soul started as an individual till today has acquired lots of impressions and built its own personality which has become my wealth, my estate. That estate has divine qualities but also some devilish qualities.
And as these verses now will describe, what are the differences between the two? So the chapter opens with the first three verses which defines all the divine qualities or 26 qualities we have seen in first three verses. These are similar to the verses we have seen before where the Kshetra Gna was described by 20 qualities. Kshetra was defined very elaborately in that chapter where Kshatragna was just given the qualities Amanittam oddam bitvam ahinsaakshantihi arjavam acharya upasana.
Because the divine can only be expressed through its own expressions. Outside my physical appearance can be described by my mind, can only be read through my actions. Expressions of my mind, through my speech, my actions.
So the divine is defined only by its expressions. And expressions we have seen in Kshatragna the Amani tum vadu. Their similar qualities are here now described as divine qualities of a being, a person.
The my estate then rest of the chapter now focuses on the devilish qualities or demoniac qualities. The reason for that is for us to know that the unique thing about ourselves is: its very easy for me to detect divine qualities in me. Also, it is very easy for me to detect devilish qualities in others.
My own devilish qualities Im either completely unaware of, or even if Im aware of them, I have justification for them. But my divine qualities Im very aware of and I can detect very easily. Well, Im a very honest person.
Im a straightforward person. All that I others see me other way around. So you ask Meena, my opinion about myself is very different than my opinion about myself.
We constantly see the demonic qualities in other but divine qualities in us. On the other hand, when I have to judge myself -- am I a divine being or a demonic being? -- Ill always say, maybe, Im not sure, Im not divine. So we are completely confused about what our real nature is all about.
So now Bhagavan clearly defines these qualities. Divine, as we said, is very easy to identify. But demonic is difficult when it comes to me. Its very easy for me to say thats not a good quality in others.
But the same behavior when I do, I will have a justification for it. So Bhagavan now goes into elaboration of why these qualities should be detected within yourself, how to detect them, and then how to avoid them. Verse 4 gave us in brief the devilish qualities.
He said: Dambhah Darpah Abhimanah Cha Krodhah Parushyam Eva Cha Agnanam Cha Abhijatasya Partha Sampadam Asurim. These qualities are born out of your Asuric Sampat. What you have acquired is not your real nature.
This Sampat is not your real nature. So as most of us at my age say, We came from India with $8 in our pocket. Everything I have here, I acquired from the United States by working here. So we were born with pristine nature, the self without any quality.
And we acquired all these qualities -- of what? So, Dambha -- hypocrisy; Darpa -- arrogance. Now there are subtle differences between them, even though we feel they all basically fall into the same behavior pattern. Dambha, hypocrisy: something which I am not, but Im projecting.
Im not a very religious person, but outwardly I try to come across as a religious person. Darpa -- arrogance, I dont care. Abhimana -- self-conceit, a greater opinion about oneself.
Abhimana. Krodha -- anger. Then Parushyam -- harshness, whether physical harshness or mental harshness.
Agnanam -- ignorance. Bhagavan says, the more I associate with this world of materialistic Prakriti, the more I lose my identity with my true self. Agnanam -- they are Abhijatasya Partha Sampadam Asurim.
They are born out of your devilish estate. The qualities which you acquire from this world by attaching yourself to the materialistic values. So in simple obviously it is defined as divine qualities are one which are spiritual and devilish quality ones which are materialistic.
So ed that the whole humankind can be divided into two those who are more divine and those who are more demonic. And then he also goes into the third kind called Raksasis. Now obviously Sid is here so you have to be careful in defining this in historical terms.
But Asuras and Raxasas were probably tribes at one point of time or Asura is actually one of the gods. Then there was a split. So people who followed Asura went to Iran, and those who remained stayed here.
But as far as the ideas here: there are people who have more divine qualities or predominant sattvic qualities, who are closer to their real self. Those with more materialistic tendencies, who give more emphasis to enjoying the material pleasures, they are called Asuras. And Rakshasas are considered those who are completely ignorant about either.
They are at the animalistic level, left on the lap of Mother Nature. They dont have self efforts to improve themselves. So Bhagawan said here that these are the qualities which are considered demonic.
Dhamba, Darpa, Abhimana, Krodha, Parushyam and Agnanam. And then rest of the chapter elaborates on the behavior and the verse 5 says Devi Sampadvi Mokshaya. Why should I be focusing on the divine? Because it will liberate you from your bondage. Bondage with the identification with your limited self.
Right now I consider myself to be the limited being. The limitedness is creating all the sorrows in my life. Im not powerful enough, Im not tall enough, Im not strong enough.
All those things which is stopping me to enjoy the unbroken happiness is because of my bondage to this limitedness. Once it is Devi Sampath Vimokshaya is for liberating you from your bondage. Nibandhaya Asuri Mata Asuri is considered to be binding you to this limitedness.
Masuchaha Sampadam daibim Abhijato Asi Bandava. But O Pandav, you dont worry, O Arjuna, dont worry. You are born with divine qualities.
And last time we had discussion about whether Bhagavan said that because you are a royal prince. It does not say anything about royal prince here. It simply says you are born with divine qualities.
Bhagavan just assured him that just the behavior you have exhibited in your life. I assure you that you are born in divine qualities. We all can be assured that we have divine qualities.
The very fact that on a Sunday morning you are learning Bhagavad Gita because of the divine quality. Giving assurance to seekers that if you are sincere about Liberating yourself, you need to have some courage. As I said, we have easy detection of a divine quality.
But when it comes to our judgment, we are not sure whether we are divine or not. So here is an assurance that because you are exhibiting divine qualities that you are divine. So the Master Chaha, do not worry.
I look back on my life and I see a lot of mistakes I made and now I am worried about whether this is my exhibition of my devilish qualities. The very fact that youre interested in liberating yourself tells you that you are exhibiting the divine quality. Continue in a path of your journey for seeking your liberation.
Now start making statements. Dvav Bhuta Sargo Loki Asmin Deva Asura Evacha Devo Vistarasahaprakhtaha Asuram Partha Meshrunaho. There are two types of beings in this world, Divine and demonic. Divine we have talked about at length in the previous chapters in Bhagavad Gita we have been talking about these divine qualities of the Supreme Being manifesting through all beings.
We have been describing in detail. Bhagawan said, so now Ill just focus on Asuri. Im going to tell you Asuri in detail now.
So rest of the chapter now focus on the behavior of Asuri. Prakriti Pravritimcha Nivruttimcha Janana Vidhu Asuraha. Very first manifestation of demonic qualities. I do not know what should be done and what should not be done, what is the right thing to do, what is not right thing to do, what I should be engaging into and what I should refrain from, what I should stay away from if I can decide that Bhagavan said, this is the first quality of your demonic estate.
No Saucam, there is no purity. Purity at the physical level, mental level, intellectual. Now Socham na cha API acharaha na satyam tesu vidyate.
Those people with demonic qualities, they do not know what to do, what not to do. They neither have purity nor right conduct. They do not know the truth.
All these things are the manifestation of demonic qualities. So now we can start looking at ourselves and say, is that something I should be detecting in myself and correcting? And with that, Ill stop here because the rest is a continuation of this discussion. We are discussing chapter 16, Deva Asura Sampath Vibhaga Yoga -- Yoga of Divine and Devilish Qualities, or Estate, or Wealth.
We have started learning Bhagavad Gita from Lord Krishna, where he first gave us this scenario of Arjuna -- that Arjuna is a broken-down hero, a person who has all the strength, all the valor, all the training to fight his situations.

Verse 7 identifies the first sign of demonic tendency: not knowing pravritti (what to engage in) and nivritti (what to refrain from). This confusion about right action was precisely Arjunas condition in Chapter 1. The teaching clarifies that such confusion is not a personal failing but the natural result of an impure mind - one lacking saucha (cleanliness), achara (right conduct), and satya (truth). When you find yourself unable to decide what is right, recognize this as a signal to purify your inner instrument through study, reflection, and disciplined practice. Ask yourself today: In what areas of my life am I genuinely confused about right action? What impurities - desires, fears, attachments - might be clouding my discrimination?
Verses 8-9 describe those who believe the universe has no underlying truth (asatya), no foundation (apratishtha), and no governing intelligence (anishvara) - that everything arose by chance from the union of opposites. Krishna calls such people alpa-buddhayah (of small intellect) and ugra-karmanah (of fierce actions). This is not condemnation but diagnosis: when I see no sacred purpose in existence, I treat life - mine and others - as expendable. Notice how your worldview shapes your behavior. When you act as if only material success matters, what becomes of your compassion, patience, and honesty? Today, consciously affirm: There is a deeper order to existence. My actions have consequences beyond what I can immediately see. Observe how this shift in perspective changes your choices, even in small matters.
